_source: Built 2026-08-13. Curated by web research (Wikimedia Commons search first per CLAUDE.md convention, falling back to hsc-norway.no -- a Norwegian high-speed-craft enthusiast archive -- Brødrene Aa's own shipbuilder site, and skipsrevyen.no's båtomtaler ferry-review section where no Commons photo existed). Every vessel below was identity-checked against this project's own data/reference/vessel_mmsi_map.json (MMSI/IMO/year-of-build/current-route), not just name-matched -- several candidate photos were rejected or flagged because Norwegian ferry names get reused/cascaded across unrelated routes decades apart (see 'identity_note' per vessel). Images copied into frontend/public/vessels/<slug>.jpg, resized to max 1400px on the long edge and re-encoded at JPEG quality 78 (via macOS `sips`) to keep the repo addition small -- originals were as large as 14MB (Commons full-resolution uploads). Two of the 18 vessels in gold_vessel_reliability.json (Lovund, Lurøy) have NO entry here: no confidently-identifiable real photo of that specific hull was found (see 'not_found' section) -- per task instructions, do not fabricate a stock photo for these.
_license_key: license values are the source's own stated license/terms where known (Commons files: their actual license tag; hsc-norway.no/skipsrevyen.no/braa.no: 'no explicit license found', i.e. ordinary copyright with no stated reuse terms -- used anyway per explicit user acceptance of that risk for this internal/private tool). attribution_credit is the photographer/site name to show in the UI tooltip; source_url is the page (not always the raw image) the photo was found on, for traceability.

Bre.identity_note: Direct name+MMSI match, no ambiguity -- same builder announcement already cited as this vessel's primary source in vessel_mmsi_map.json.

Herøysund.attribution_credit: Photo: Svein Bj, via Wikimedia Commons
Herøysund.identity_note: Only one Norwegian ferry named Herøysund; independently confirmed via skipsrevyen.no's own vessel-review page (skipsrevyen.no/mf-heroysund) as one of the Stokkvågen-Lovund-Træna route's 4 sister vessels, christened 2013 alongside Husøy/Lovund/Tenna.

Husøy.photo_caption: RORO passenger ferry Husøy (IMO 9663403) in harbor at Husøya, Træna archipelago, Nordland, 17 May 2023
Husøy.identity_note: Caption states IMO 9663403 and MMSI 258695000 explicitly -- exact match to vessel_mmsi_map.json's Husøy entry, taken at one of this project's own route's real quays (before its 2025-10-12 reassignment to Hasvik-Øksfjord).

Tenna.attribution_credit: Photo: Svein Bj, via Wikimedia Commons
Tenna.identity_note: Only one Norwegian ferry named Tenna in this size/class; independently confirmed via skipsrevyen.no's own vessel-review page as one of the same 4 Helgeland sister vessels (christened 2013 alongside Husøy/Lovund/Herøysund). vessel_mmsi_map.json flags this specific hull as 'unresolved' for the Stokkvågen-Lovund-Træna route in the 2025 window (AIS evidence puts it in Troms all year) -- this photo is still a correct, real photo of the physical ship named Tenna, just not evidence it operated this route in 2025.

Sigrid.identity_note: Commons filename embeds IMO 9030369, cross-checked live: vesseltracker.com/vesselfinder both resolve IMO 9030369 to MMSI 257243500, home port Sandnessjøen, operator Boreal Sjø -- exact match to vessel_mmsi_map.json's Sigrid entry. Photo predates its move to the Sandnessjøen area (Korsfjorden is near Bergen) but is confirmed the same hull.

Folgefonn.attribution_credit: Photo: Harald Sætre, via Wikimedia Commons
Folgefonn.photo_caption: MF Folgefonn, built 1998, en route between Hatvik and Vengjaneset (Hordaland), 1998
Folgefonn.identity_note: MEDIUM confidence: matched on name + exact build year (1998) + vessel class (76-car symmetrical shuttle ferry), corroborated by independent web search confirming MF Folgefonn (1998-built, 76 cars/200 passengers) is the named main vessel on the Sandnessjøen-Dønna-Løkta route today. No IMO cross-check was available for this vessel in vessel_mmsi_map.json to confirm the exact same hull (unlike Høgsfjord/Hjelmeland/Sigrid/Sjernarøy below). Two other, older, unrelated ferries also named Folgefonn exist on Commons (1930s/40s Hardanger vessels) and were excluded -- this is the only 1998-built one. Photo predates the vessel's move to Nordland (taken in Hardanger, its original service area) -- same likely reasoning as the Rogaland-origin vessels below (cascaded north after retirement from a busier route), but treat this identification as slightly less certain than the others in this file.

Sjernaroy.attribution_credit: Photo: Toyni Tobekk, via Wikimedia Commons
Sjernaroy.identity_note: Cross-checked live: marinetraffic.com/vesselfinder/myshiptracking all resolve IMO 9192480 to MMSI 259593000, current location Sandnessjøen -- exact match to vessel_mmsi_map.json's Sjernaroy entry (built 1999). Photo predates its move north (Hebnes/Ryfylke is in Rogaland, the ferry's namesake and original service area, Sjernarøyane) but is confirmed the same hull via IMO.

Vikingen.attribution_credit: Photo: Marius Vassnes, via Wikimedia Commons
Vikingen.identity_note: Cross-checked: Norwegian Wikipedia's MF «Vikingen» (1992) article confirms a car ferry built 1992 for Hardanger Sunnhordlandske Dampskipsselskap that later served Stavanger-Tau (2006-2012) and Skjersholmane-Ranavik (2017-2019) before Fjord1 took over that route -- and an Alamy stock photo independently places 'Norled MF Vikingen' at Sandnessjøen, matching vessel_mmsi_map.json's reserve-vessel-for-Sandnessjøen-Dønna-Løkta entry. This 2021 Commons photo (Bjørnafjorden, near Bergen) is from during that transition period, same hull.

Høgsfjord.attribution_credit: Photo: Hallvard Nygård, via Wikimedia Commons
Høgsfjord.photo_caption: MF Høgsfjord at the quay in Lauvik, Rogaland, 18 August 2006
Høgsfjord.identity_note: Cross-checked live: vesselfinder.com/marinetraffic.com both resolve IMO 9055759 to MMSI 257288400 -- exact match to vessel_mmsi_map.json's Høgsfjord entry (built 1992, main vessel on the Søvik-Herøy route). The vessel is named for Høgsfjorden, a Rogaland fjord it originally served (Lauvik-Oanes) -- this 2006 photo is from that original posting, before its later relocation to the Helgeland coast (Søvik-Herøy) as older tonnage cascaded north. Same physical hull, confirmed by IMO.

Hjelmeland.attribution_credit: Photo: Svein Bj, via Wikimedia Commons
Hjelmeland.identity_note: IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION (flagged in vessel_mmsi_map.json itself): 'Hjelmeland' is also the name of an unrelated Rogaland ferry route (Hjelmeland-Nesvik-Skipavik) that historically used a same-named vessel -- but this Commons file was reached via Wikimedia's own 'Category:IMO 9055747', and vesselfinder.com/marinetraffic.com independently confirm IMO 9055747 = MMSI 257282400, an exact match to vessel_mmsi_map.json's Hjelmeland entry (built 1993, sister ship to Høgsfjord, moved to the Søvik-Herøy route October 2024). Same cascading-relocation pattern as Høgsfjord/Sjernarøy/Vikingen above: this photo is from the vessel's original Rogaland posting, same confirmed hull.

Lovund.note: No confidently-identifiable real photo found. Searched Wikimedia Commons (name and IMO 9664471 category, both empty), skipsrevyen.no's båtomtaler (the combined Husøy-Lovund review page's only image is captioned as sister ship Herøysund, not Lovund itself), ferry-site.dk (has no separate Lovund entry found), shipspotting.com, and Norwegian Wikipedia's route article (only has a harbor photo, no vessel photo). Not fabricated -- left without an image per task instructions.

Luroy.note: No confidently-identifiable real, freely-reusable photo found. ferry-site.dk (ferry.php?id=9221047) has 4 real photos credited to Frans Truyens, but that site explicitly states 'Photos on this site may not be used on other websites... without written permission from the photographer' -- a direct prohibition on exactly this reuse, so not used despite being a real, identified photo of this specific hull (IMO 9221047). No other source with a usable photo was found (Commons IMO 9221047 category is empty; skipsrevyen.no has no dedicated Lurøy review page). Left without an image rather than violate the source's explicit terms.
